interaction.user_prompt: T-5.3.3 UAT bug: Ctrl+C after Insert-selecting copies the cursor entry, not the selection (branch feature/T-5.3.3-clipboard, PR #74)
interaction.model_cot:
Owner's UAT: Insert selects and advances the cursor (TC behaviour), so after selecting two files the cursor sits on the third, unselected entry; Ctrl+C then copied that third file. Cause: the "act on the selection only when the cursor entry is itself selected" rule I introduced for Open/Open With (PR #72) and reused for the clipboard. That rule is Explorer's context-menu semantics, not TC's: in TC every selection-aware command (F5/F6/F8, and the clipboard) acts on the selection whenever one exists and falls back to the cursor entry only when nothing is selected -- exactly what this codebase's own `copy_move_dialog::resolve_source_names` already implements for F5/F6. Decision: one rule everywhere, selection wins when non-empty; `selection_or_cursor_info` drops the cursor-in-selection condition, so Ctrl+C/X, Open, Open With and the palette all agree with F5/F6. Consequence accepted: right-clicking an unselected row while a selection exists acts on the selection (TC's own context menu does the same). Regression test reproduces the owner's exact steps: Insert, Insert, cursor lands on the third row, Ctrl+C yields the two selected paths.
